newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Europe awaits Ivorian crop as cocoa trickles in.
newsitem.headline: Europe awaits Ivorian crop as cocoa trickles in.

text.p: The start of cocoa shipments from Nigeria and Cameroon has given Europe's physical market small amounts to trade, but most eyes are focused on when main crop beans from Ivory Coast will arrive.

Traders said they believed the main crop this year would be around 900,000 tonnes, slightly larger than initial projections, and would be a little late in leaving the ports of the world's largest producer.
"It's pretty quiet in Europe but there's some Nigerian and Cameroon cocoa around and it won't pick up until the Ivorian shipments start rolling in," one trader said.
Officially, the Ivorian season is due to open on October 15.
Amsterdam warehouse sources said they expected the first cocoa to arrive from Ivory Coast in early to mid-December.

Paul Naar, managing director at Gerkens Cacoa, part of U.S. trading house Cargill, told Reuters the company had not yet formulated its shipping plans as the export situation in Ivory Coast was still unclear.
"We're still waiting for news from our shipping sources on when the season will start," he said.
Gerkens has experimented with bulk shipments of cocoa beans earlier this year, describing the first trials as successful. It hopes to increase tonnages shipped this way in 1996/97.
But other traders said they expected only a minor delay to the coming Ivorian main crop and that cocoa would be arriving into European store houses in mid to late November.

Spectacular third quarter grind figures from the UK and the Netherlands, and to a slightly lesser extent from Germany, reinforced the view that processing in Western Europe was roaring ahead on the back of good Eastern European demand and steady consumption throughout the continent's cool summer.

Stocks in the Dutch capital have dwindled as a result. The latest figures from warehousing group SGS Europe show Amsterdam inventories at just above 430,000 tonnes, well below the 500,000 plus recorded during the summer.
